findings_and_relationships.classification: conditional source-level cache availability question; no observed failure or supported browser reachability established
findings_and_relationships.first_contract: When IndexedDB is enabled, cache.get computes SHA-256 for the job address before the guarded storage transaction. A rejection/throw from that digest, or from checksum digest on an existing record, escapes cache.get; coordinator resolveJob does not catch it, the pool closes and rethrows, and preparation is cancelled rather than regenerating as an optional-cache miss.
findings_and_relationships.conditions: The cache is enabled and a subsequent crypto.subtle.digest invocation for a job key or existing stored checksum throws or rejects, despite successful startup. Normal renderer startup already requires an initial SHA-256 digest of the Wasm binary, so a browser wholly lacking crypto.subtle fails earlier and is not an established ordinary path to this cache case. Actual supported browser API, intermittent platform failure, runtime reuse and alternate callers are uninspected; no crypto fault or failed scene was observed.
findings_and_relationships.safeguards: Missing IndexedDB, blocked open and transaction timeouts use explicit cache-unavailable/miss paths; malformed product decoding is evicted only for specific Rust product errors. Writes are deferred and failure reported separately, not on this lookup path. Prior SHA-256 over stored bytes checks integrity but is not authentication.
findings_and_relationships.relationship: q1899 is the broader original product-address/cache boundary obligation; prior worker-trust and 774 CONT07-560/SEGOVB-INITIAL04-581 summaries are related but do not establish this particular digest-rejection first cut. The old operations summary that optional-cache failure does not gate readiness did not document this escaping pre-transaction call; preserve that as an older qualified summary, not a retroactive historical finding. Central decides final aliases and whether this supported-failure policy is actionable.
findings_and_relationships.future_repair_direction: After the audit gate, decide the browser crypto/readiness contract and distinguish optional-cache-only digest failures from mandatory Wasm product or dependency failures; preserve typed invalid-product eviction and authoritative Rust admission.

nonfindings_and_open_questions: Cache key uses cache format, executable digest and exact opaque Rust job text; record revision, compressed checksum and decoded length bounds are checked. A matching checksum establishes stored-byte consistency, not authenticated provenance or internal product geometry validity.

Worker messages require safe positive dispatch identity; pool rejects malformed or mismatched kinds, ignores messages for other dispatches, checks transferable bytes and nonnegative timing, and closes/terminates workers on failure. No browser Worker behavior or timeout was tested.

Wasm receive independently parses the exact job and typed CBOR, checks ticket owner and product variant plus specific identity fields. Complete mesh/city semantic validation and every consumer remain separate earlier assessment scope (q1308–1310, q1385).

Rust job discovery, dynamic dependency ordering, all runtime call sites and external cache/document concurrency remain open; no fabricated worker fixture, callback race or unsupported malformed product is asserted.

Deferred queue accounts for underlying full allocation and UTF-16 job, retains/replaces in a bounded map, transfers after synchronous Wasm receipt, drains bounded write lanes and collects failures. Prior 774 reports distinguish a general async-callback race from actual synchronous coordinator behavior.

A record written after another document’s inventory snapshot can be missed until a later cache opening by stated source/documentation policy; a false miss is not established stale-authoritative product behavior.
Embedded current-source assertions, native libraries, APIs, executable profiles and renderer runtime were not run; no test/build/browser/worker/simulation/shader or product validation performed.

lens_notes.producer_propagation: Opaque job/compiled revision -> worker generated bytes -> Wasm receipt -> deferred cache; cache-only digest failure is conditional and distinct from mandatory product admission.
lens_notes.type_ownership: Rust owns generation job/product identity and PreparationError codes, while JS owns native Worker/IndexedDB dispatch and diagnostic boundaries; exact semantic coverage of all payloads remains open.
lens_notes.type_granularity: Preparation ticket, dispatch ordinal, job identity, executable digest and cache integrity hash have distinct roles; no one identifier substitutes for all others.
lens_notes.admission_contracts: Pool validates dispatch and transferred response, queue validates safe integer budgets and buffer type, cache bounds recorded and decoded lengths, Rust checks job/product ownership/variant identity.
lens_notes.invariant_operations: Queue replaces charges without losing ownership and drains under finite lane limits; compressed bytes may exceed the decoded size limit as previously noted. Hash failure is not converted to an optional cache miss.
lens_notes.enum_shapes: Worker status/kind/reason strings are internal JS protocol tags; they select checked paths but are not evidence of a required Rust enum migration.
lens_notes.aggregate_states: Revision, exact job, serialized typed product and receipt must agree; cached checksum and data are independently stored, so integrity is not provenance. Scene preparation ticket ownership remains mandatory.
lens_notes.magic_numbers: Worker cap4, timeouts 2/30/180 seconds and product/cache byte budgets each bound a separate operation; policy and native scheduling assumptions need actual owner review, not blanket replacement.
lens_notes.magic_strings: CACHE_FORMAT, IndexedDB names, Rust exception codes and Worker message kinds are native protocol values; distinguish typed upstream semantic errors from final human messages.
lens_notes.existing_type_owners: Reuse Rust GenerationJob, Product and PreparationTicket at their actual serialization boundaries; do not independently parse job text in JS for semantic classification.
lens_notes.redundant_authority: Do not conflate executable revision, content checksum or dispatch sequencing. Cache inventory is a deliberately stale index for false misses; no extra authoritative simulation state is established.
lens_notes.behavior_preservation: Preserve cold generation when storage is unavailable, checked wrong-product eviction, cancellation, receiver-before-transfer order and nonblocking optional writes; startup SHA requirement has its own contract.
lens_notes.derivability: Simple JS data records and Rust typed product checks were observed; no redundant hand-written trait/serialization rewrite was established in this bounded source scope.

limitations.evidence_only: Read-only Git/source inspection and evidence JSON/gzip/hash verification only. No product edits, JS or worker execution, builds, tests, browser, runtime probes, simulations or shaders.
limitations.publication: Central owns baseline, cross-lens reconciliation, connected ledger and checkpoint publication. 059 and 774 records keep their original revisions and qualifications; none is promoted to checkpoint3821.
